items.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016
items.q: I think Ron Carter and Grady Tate I want to say or somebody on drums.

ctx.x: And the little arrangements they had behind her. I’m a big, basically both of them, Adderley nut. And I used to think when I would listen to their stuff a lot of times they would do a lot of stuff in unison. And I always thought boy if I was arranging that I would have done a harmony. Well that’s why they’re who they are. They sort of knew that. It sounded like one voice.

Yeah. And you’d go to see them and there was a high mic and a low mic. And Cannonball would play on the high mic, and Nat, who was much smaller, would play on the low mic. Right? Oh man, yeah, I’m a huge fan. You know we were talking about Gene Bertoncini who is a huge fan. He got to do a record with Nancy Wilson, it’s called “But Beautiful.” And it was Gene and Hank Jones and I think Ron Carter and Grady Tate I want to say or somebody on drums. And they did it, no solos. Hank may play eight bars

here or there. The tunes are super short. And they finished it and they were going to add strings and they listened to it and they decided not to because it’s just so great. And that was such a credit to Gene that he got to do that kind of stuff and he was such a great accompanist and such a great player.
